\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{marginnote}
\usepackage{sidenotes}
\title{An Invented Survey of Margins}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
An invented survey of margins opens here with plain running text about
nothing in particular, set only so that a note has a line to stand
by.\marginpar{Kite note, long enough to wrap in its column.}
The paragraph runs on with more made up words, and a second note follows
close behind.\marginpar{Plover note.} Its last line ends the paragraph.

\marginpar{Heron note.}
Another paragraph of synthetic remarks follows, carrying a ragged
note\marginnote{Wren note.} and a numbered one\sidenote{Lark note.} before
it ends.

\reversemarginpar
The reversed note stands in the other margin.\marginpar{Swift note.}
\end{document}
